content: 1. Data was collected through self-reported measures as well as a review of clinical records by data clerks at both study facilities and surrounding facilities. 2. The evidence was downgraded due to two reasons: (1) the presence of a large confidence interval, and (2) the confidence interval crossing the line of no effect. 3. Results from one study were adjusted for cluster effects using the intraclass correlation coefficient reported in the study. 4. The evidence was downgraded once due to the potential for performance bias, as there was a lack of blinding in the trials. However, detection bias was rated as low because linkage to care was measured using both self-reported data and clinical record reviews. 5. The evidence was further downgraded because the denominator used was not the intention-to-treat (ITT) population (those enrolled in the study) but rather those who tested positive. 6. Cluster effects were not adjusted for in some cases, but the risk of bias (RoB) was already rated at the lowest level. 7. The evidence was downgraded once due to the potential for performance bias (lack of blinding) in all trials and a high risk of detection bias in one trial, where outcomes were self-reported. 8. In three trials, the risk of detection bias was unclear. 9. The risk of selection bias was unclear in three trials. 10. Reporting bias was unclear in one trial, as outcomes specified in the trial registry were not reported in the manuscript. 11. Heterogeneity in the results was driven by one study with non-significant results. This heterogeneity may be explained by population differences, as one study was conducted in the general population, while others targeted specific populations such as truck drivers and female sex workers. 12. The evidence was downgraded due to very large confidence intervals and because three out of four confidence intervals crossed the line of no effect. 13. Subgroup analysis further downgraded the risk of bias, as the effect was no longer randomized. 14. The evidence was downgraded once due to large confidence intervals. 15. In one study, results were adjusted for cluster effects using the reported intraclass correlation coefficient. 16. The evidence was downgraded once due to the potential for performance bias (lack of blinding) and a high risk of detection bias in one trial with self-reported outcomes. 17. No participants in the facility-based HIV self-testing (FB-HIVST) arm reported coercion to test (n = 0/1052). 18. No participants in the FB-HIVST arm reported coercion to disclose test results (n = 0/1052). However, one participant in the standard of care (SOC) arm (n = 1/248) and three participants in the optimized SOC arm (n = 3/261) reported coercion to disclose test results. 19. The evidence was downgraded once due to the potential for performance bias (lack of blinding) and a high risk of detection bias in one trial with self-reported outcomes. 20. The risk of detection bias was unclear in three trials. 21. The risk of selection bias was unclear in three trials. 22. Reporting bias was unclear in one trial, as outcomes specified in the trial registry were not reported in the manuscript. 23. The evidence was further downgraded because the denominator used was not the ITT population but rather the number of participants who tested for HIV, excluding those with previously known HIV-positive status. 24. Cluster effects were not adjusted for, but the RoB was already rated at the lowest level. 25.
